prompt: In `pl confusion`, what does a row hold?
hint: Rows and columns are two different people's answers.

choices.text: The messages with one person's label
choices.why: Right, spread by the label the reply gave: the row is the truth, the columns are the replies.

choices.text: The messages that the reply gave one particular label to
choices.why: That is a column.

choices.text: One message's five samples, side by side
choices.why: This run has one call per message.

choices.text: The checks a reply passed
choices.why: That is `pl check`.

prompt: In the category matrix for `v6-escaped.txt`, how many messages did the prompt sort as delivery, right or wrong?
hint: Add up the `delivery` column.

prompt: In the same matrix, how many of the messages the prompt called `other` were not `other`?
hint: Precision for other is 0.67, and the diagonal cell is 8.

prompt: Account has recall 0.64 and precision 1.00. What does that pair say?
hint: Read one along a row, the other down a column.

choices.text: The prompt is good at account and nothing needs fixing
choices.why: Five account messages never reach the account team.

choices.text: Account labels in the test set are wrong
choices.why: Nothing in the matrix says so.

choices.text: Every account message was found, but some were wrong
choices.why: That is the opposite pair: high recall, low precision.

choices.text: When it says account it is right, and it says it too rarely
choices.why: Right: nine of nine called account were, and nine of fourteen were found.

prompt: Urgency accuracy is 54 of 70. Why does the lesson say that number is not enough?
hint: Compare `h03` with a low question sorted normal.

choices.text: It counts a missed urgent message the same as a harmless one
choices.why: Right: six high sorted normal cost far more than seven low sorted normal.

choices.text: It includes the two format failures, so it is too low
choices.why: They are counted, but that is not the argument.

choices.text: Urgency should be measured with recall only and never with accuracy
choices.why: Recall alone can be gamed by calling everything high.

choices.text: Seventy messages are too few
choices.why: The problem is what the number weighs, not the sample.

prompt: `t26` has the right category and urgency inside a code fence. How should it be counted?
hint: Which fix would it need?

choices.text: As a correct answer, since the content is right
choices.why: A program cannot use it; it fails `json`.

choices.text: As a format failure, apart from wrong labels
choices.why: Right: it lands in `(bad)`, not in a billing cell.

choices.text: As a billing message sorted wrongly
choices.why: Its label was right; the wrapping was wrong.

choices.text: It should be removed from the test set
choices.why: Its failure is information.

prompt: Of the 14 replies that fail `category` under `v6-escaped.txt`, how many parsed and chose the wrong label?
hint: Two never parsed.

prompt: Why can a format rate be measured in production when accuracy cannot?
hint: What does accuracy need that format does not?

choices.text: Production replies are always valid JSON
choices.why: They are not; that is why it is worth measuring.

choices.text: It needs no person's label
choices.why: Right: a live message has no `expect`.

choices.text: Format checks run faster than a model call
choices.why: True, but speed is not what makes it possible.

choices.text: Accuracy needs temperature 0
choices.why: Temperature is unrelated.

prompt: How many of the twelve drafts pass every tone rule?
hint: Count the `ok` lines.

prompt: `t02` promises to write again *by Thursday*, and the `promise` rule did not flag it. Why?
hint: Read `checks/tone.json`.

choices.text: Thursday is not on its list
choices.why: Right: a rule catches exactly what it names.

choices.text: The exclamation rule failed first and stopped the others
choices.why: `pl tone` applies every rule; `t12` fails two.

choices.text: A date is not a promise in this domain
choices.why: A date a customer is told is a commitment.

choices.text: The rule ignores replies that thank the customer
choices.why: Nothing in the rule looks at thanks.

prompt: `t03` fails `promise` for *a replacement goes out today*. What kind of error is that, if same-day replacements are normal at the shop?
hint: Is anything wrong with the sentence?

choices.text: A missed promise the rule should have caught
choices.why: It was flagged, not missed.

choices.text: A correct flag on a risky sentence
choices.why: If the shop does it, the sentence is fine.

choices.text: A false positive
choices.why: Right: the proxy and the judgement part ways.

choices.text: A format failure caused by the word today
choices.why: Drafts are prose; there is no format check.

prompt: A rule stands in for a judgement it cannot make, so a rule is a ___ for that judgement.
hint: A stand-in measure.

prompt: Why is the `promise` rule a safety check in this domain rather than a style note?
hint: Who is bound by what a reply says?

choices.text: Because promises make replies longer
choices.why: Length has its own rule.

choices.text: Because customers dislike promises
choices.why: They like them; the shop may not keep them.

choices.text: Because a promise in a prompt is an injection
choices.why: These are replies, not prompts.

choices.text: A reply commits the shop to what it promises
choices.why: Right: `t12`'s refund in 24 hours is owed once it is sent.

prompt: A team cuts its leak rate to zero by refusing every message that contains *ignore*. What has it forgotten to measure?
hint: Think of `a07`.

choices.text: The leak rate at a higher temperature
choices.why: Zero is zero; the missing number is elsewhere.

choices.text: The honest messages it now refuses
choices.why: Right: a safety metric in one direction improves by doing less.

choices.text: The cost of the extra check
choices.why: A string search costs next to nothing.

choices.text: Whether the canary is still in the prompt
choices.why: Unrelated to refusals.

prompt: Which of these are safety metrics in the sense of this lesson? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three kinds were named, in two directions.

choices.text: Replies that promise something the shop did not agree
choices.why: Yes: the `promise` rule.

choices.text: Replies that repeat the canary
choices.why: Yes: a leak of the prompt.

choices.text: Honest messages refused
choices.why: Yes: the other direction.

choices.text: Replies with more than one exclamation mark
choices.why: That is tone, not safety.

prompt: `v3-examples.txt` sorted 23 messages as billing. How many of those were not billing?
hint: The diagonal cell for billing is 14.

prompt: `v3` and `v6` both sort 56 of 70 correctly. Which statement is supported by the metrics?
hint: Look at format and at the billing column.

choices.text: They are equivalent, since the accuracy is the same
choices.why: Same accuracy, different mistakes.

choices.text: `v6` is better at everything
choices.why: `v3` parses every reply and `v6` does not.

choices.text: `v3` parses better; `v6` is far more precise on billing
choices.why: Right: 70 against 68 parsed, and 0.61 against 0.87.

choices.text: `v3` is better at everything, because none of its replies fail format
choices.why: Nine of its billing tickets belong to someone else.

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer a gate on high-sorted-as-normal to a weight on it inside a combined score?
hint: What can a weight be traded against?

choices.text: Gates are easier to compute
choices.why: Both are trivial arithmetic.

choices.text: A gain elsewhere cannot buy back a gate
choices.why: Right: a threshold on one metric cannot be offset.

choices.text: Weights only work for format
choices.why: Weights work for anything; that is the problem.

choices.text: Urgency cannot be measured as a number
choices.why: It was: recall 0.62 for high.

prompt: Match each metric to the question it answers.
hint: One each.

pairs.right: Of the real account messages, how many were found?
Of the replies saying delivery, how many were right?
How many replies could a program use?
Does a reply commit the shop to something?

right_distractors: Which prompt is cheaper per call?

prompt: A new prompt raises urgency accuracy from 54 to 56 of 70, and high-urgency recall falls from 0.62 to 0.50. What do you report?
hint: Which cell is the expensive one?

choices.text: An improvement of two messages, so ship it
choices.why: The two gained hide the urgent ones lost.

choices.text: Nothing until the format rate is known
choices.why: Format is worth reporting, but it does not answer this.

choices.text: That more urgent messages are now missed
choices.why: Right, whatever accuracy did: name the expensive cell, and gate on it.

choices.text: A tie, since the two changes cancel each other out
choices.why: They cost different amounts; they do not cancel.
